memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Lamech had lived 182 years, he had a son. He named him Noah and said, "He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground the Lord has cursed." After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters. Altogether, Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died. - Gen 5:28-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This Lamech is very different from the boastful Lamech of Cain's line. When his son is born, he speaks not of vengeance but of longing - a deep yearning for comfort and rest. He names his son Noah, meaning "rest" or "comfort," and expresses the ache of a world still groaning under the curse: "the labor and painful toil... caused by the ground the Lord has cursed."

Here is a father who feels the weight of living in a fallen world and hopes that his son might bring some relief. It is a heartfelt cry that many of us understand - the longing for rest from the endless toil and sorrow of life under the curse.

Lamech's hope in Noah was partly fulfilled; through Noah, God preserved the human race and gave the earth a fresh start. But no mere man could lift the curse or give the soul its deepest rest.

That rest would come only through One greater than Noah. Jesus said, "Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest" (Matt 11:28). The longing Lamech felt is finally answered in Christ, who bore the curse for us (Gal 3:13) and who will one day make all things new, with no more toil, no more tears (Rev 21:4). Bring your weariness to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where do you feel the weight of living in a fallen world?
- Have you brought your weariness to Jesus, who gives true rest?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, I feel the toil and groaning of this fallen world, and I long for rest. Thank You that You bore the curse for me and offer rest to my weary soul. I come to You.
